messages.subject: Performance of different versions
parts:
This isn't a problem, just a curious observation.

I have discovered a difference in the performance of different versions of lavaan, and I wanted to share it. In my SEM course, the first homework is to reproduce a model from Bagozzi (1980) (attached). The paper includes sample moments--correlations, standard deviations, means. One observed variable (the single indicator of "performance") has a variance of about 44,000, while the variance of other variable are in single digits. That difference in scale creates problems for SEM. (The Mplus manual contains a specific warning about such situations.) The model also includes 2 single indicators. Last year, in demo-ing this kind of problem for my students using lavaan 0.5-17, I did this:

1. Analyzed correlation matrix: Result: no problem
2. Analyzed covariance matrix: Result: nonconvergence
3. Divided the standard deviation of the performance indicator by 100 (which divides its variance by 10,000) and analyze this partly rescaled covariance matrix. Result: nonconvergence.
4. Set nonzero residual variance for the two single indicators in the model (using 10% of the indicator's total variance) and analyzed the partly rescaled covariance matrix. Result: it runs, but obviously estimates are affected by the nonzero residual variances.

I am attaching an edited transcript. Unfortunately, I don't have sessionInfo(), but I ran this in September of 2015. I am attaching an edited transcript and afiles with moment matrices and syntax.

I am sending this note because I demo-ed the same model again yesterday, with this sessionInfo():

 The difference from the session with lavaan 0.5-17 was that step #3 succeeded producing the same chi-square and same (standardized) parameter estimates as step #1 previously. Edited transcript attached.

So I thought the difference in results across lavaan versions might be interesting. The laptop I used is also different (Windows 10 v Windows 7, with more RAM etc.) but I doubt that made any difference.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: Re: Performance of different versions
parts:
> The difference from the session with lavaan 0.5-17 was that step #3
> succeeded producing the same chi-square and same (standardized)
> parameter estimates as step #1 previously.

I hope I can take this as an example that lavaan improves, version after
version.

The only reason for this, is the better starting value (in 0.5-21) for
the factor variance of VerbInt.

In 0.5-17, the starting value is 0.05 (which is the default value for
all factor variances).

In 0.5-21, the starting value is 13.213, which is in fact already the
final value. We can 'guess' this value in this case, simply because this
factor only has a single indicator, and its factor loading is fixed to one.

I ran this with 0.5-17, but giving it the right starting value, and it
also converges:

fit <- sem(c(Bag.model, "VerbInt ~~ start(13.213)*VerbInt"),sample.cov =
Bagcov.100,sample.nobs = 122)
> fit
lavaan (0.5-17) converged normally after 116 iterations

Number of observations 122

Estimator ML
Minimum Function Test Statistic 15.183
Degrees of freedom 13
P-value (Chi-square) 0.296

One day, a future version of lavaan will also convergence when the
original (badly scaled) covariance matrix is used. Once I have found a
universal way to deal with scaling.

Yves.
